ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital mass with exophthalmia, hemifacial pain, and visual impairment
salient_findings: Slowly progressive orbital mass
Left exophthalmia with vision impairment and complete restriction of ocular motility
Discrete medial bulging of the left nasal fossa lateral wall and leftward septal deviation
Bone discontinuity of the maxillary, septal, sphenoid, ethmoidal walls, and pterygopalatine fossa
Heterogeneously enhancing mass in the left maxillary sinus, nasal cavity, ethmoidal sinuses, and intraorbital region
key_facts: 65-year-old woman
5-month history of orbital mass
Poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years
Stage IIB cervical adenocarcinoma treated 3 years earlier
Well-controlled hypertension, dyslipidemia, and hypothyroidism
Left exophthalmia with vision impairment and complete restriction of ocular motility
Discrete medial bulging of the left nasal fossa lateral wall and leftward septal deviation
Bone discontinuity of the maxillary, septal, sphenoid, ethmoidal walls, and pterygopalatine fossa
Heterogeneously enhancing mass on MRI
Bone disruption of the lateral and inferior orbital walls
Extension through the inferior orbital fissure
Invasion of the left cavernous sinus
Diffusion restriction around the ophthalmic nerve
Anterior displacement of the extraocular muscles and vessels
HbA1c 8.8%
CRP 15.5 mg/L
ESR 120 mm/h
Positive anti-HBc

per_call: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus

shortlist.label: Nasal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive orbital mass with bone destruction and invasion of surrounding structures, consistent with lymphoma

shortlist.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive orbital mass with exophthalmia and visual impairment, suggestive of highly aggressive malignancy

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus
shortlist.why_kept: Orbital mass with bone destruction and extension into surrounding sinuses, consistent with squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive orbital mass with invasion of surrounding structures, including the cavernous sinus, consistent with esthesioneuroblastoma

shortlist.label: Lymphoma of the orbit
shortlist.why_kept: Probable low-grade lymphoproliferative lesion on biopsy, consistent with orbital lymphoma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a rapidly progressive orbital mass, bone destruction, and invasion of surrounding structures, along with laboratory findings of elevated CRP and ESR, is consistent with an aggressive lymphoma. The presence of a heterogeneously enhancing mass on MRI and the patient's history of cervical adenocarcinoma treated with radiotherapy also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
rejected.why: While this diagnosis could explain the aggressive nature of the tumor, it is less likely given the patient's laboratory findings and the presence of a probable low-grade lymphoproliferative lesion on biopsy.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely given the patient's biopsy results and the absence of specific risk factors such as tobacco use.

rejected.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely given the patient's age and the absence of specific symptoms such as anosmia.

rejected.label: Lymphoma of the orbit
rejected.why: While this diagnosis could explain some of the patient's symptoms, it is less likely given the extent of the tumor's invasion into surrounding structures and the presence of a probable low-grade lymphoproliferative lesion on biopsy of the maxillary sinus.
